question: What will be the percentage change in the US dollar to Chinese yuan exchange rate (USDCNY=X on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-09-17 to the close on 2026-10-10?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-10-10 / close on 2026-09-17 - 1), using daily closes of USDCNY=X on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-10-10, the last close before it is used.
baseline:
Computed by code from Yahoo Finance daily closes for USDCNY=X: latest close 6.7074 on 2026-09-17.
Target date 2026-10-10 is 16 trading observations ahead. Percentiles of the price on the target date,
from the empirical distribution of 16-observation returns over the last 3 years (last year weighted double):
p5: 6.626, p10: 6.6412, p25: 6.6672, p50: 6.6907, p75: 6.717, p90: 6.7437, p95: 6.7748
This ignores news and known events; adjust for them. Check the symbol matches the resolution source
(exchange, contract month, close vs settlement price).
research:
I couldn't load Yahoo Finance or the other data pages directly: the proxy refused every fetch. Everything below comes from search-result summaries. I left out anything dated after 2026-09-19.

## 1. Resolution source
- I could not get a reading from the source itself. Yahoo's USDCNY=X history page refused the connection, so I have no exact Yahoo close for 2026-09-17. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/USDCNY=X/history/)
- 2026-09-17: An aggregator lists the close at about 6.7075, with a day range of 6.7064 to 6.7109. Gate.com cites an onshore close of 6.7085, down 21 pips. The Yahoo close is probably about 6.706 to 6.709. [exchangerates.org.uk](https://www.exchangerates.org.uk/USD-CNY-spot-exchange-rates-history-2026.html), [Gate](https://www.gate.com/news/detail/offshore-yuan-rises-to-66967-per-dollar-hits-highest-intraday-level-since-24361371)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The window runs about 16 trading days.
- 2026-09-18 (Fri): The onshore yuan moved past 6.7 per dollar and touched 6.6853 intraday, its strongest since June 2022, then gave back some gains into the close. That puts USDCNY roughly 0.1% to 0.3% below the Sept 17 baseline, but I couldn't find the exact close. [Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-09-18/yuan-surges-past-67-per-dollar-to-three-year-high-102486356.html)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-18: Caixin gives three reasons for the rally: eight straight days of stronger PBOC fixings, corporate dollar selling, and a trade surplus above $800B in Jan to Aug. The move defied expectations that the yuan would weaken after the Fed hike. [Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-09-18/yuan-surges-past-67-per-dollar-to-three-year-high-102486356.html)
- Mid-Sept 2026: Reports say the PBOC had set its daily midpoint weaker than market estimates for almost a year. This month it appears to have changed course and is letting the midpoint strengthen faster ahead of a Trump-Xi summit. [Arise](https://www.arise.tv/yuan-climbs-to-three-year-high-as-china-eases-resistance-to-currency-gains-ahead-of-trump-xi-summit/)
- 2026-09-16: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75% to 4.00%, its first hike since 2023, in a unanimous vote. Projections show one more hike by December. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose 0.5%, its biggest gain since June 17. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-16/dollar-jumps-after-fed-raises-rates-sends-hawkish-signal), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html)
- 2026-09-09: USD/CNY was about 6.7080, down from 6.7224 on Sept 1. [Currencybeacon](https://currencybeacon.com/index.php/rates/USD/CNY)
- 2026-08-20: The PBOC set a weaker-than-expected fixing to slow the yuan's gains. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/pboc-moves-to-slow-yuan-gains-with-weaker-than-expected-fixing)
- 2026-08-11: Analysts expected seasonal factors, such as strong autumn exports, to restart the yuan's rise in September. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-11/yuan-s-recent-calm-may-end-on-seasonal-factors-analysts-say)

## 4. Base rates
- The trend is steady yuan appreciation. USD/CNY was about 7.12 in September 2025 and about 6.71 in mid-September 2026, roughly -5.8% over a year. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/exchus) My own rough math: that pace works out to about -0.3% to -0.4% per 3 weeks.
- Within that trend, moves are small and slow. September went from about 6.722 (Sept 1) to about 6.708 (Sept 17), around -0.2% in two and a half weeks. [Currencybeacon](https://currencybeacon.com/index.php/rates/USD/CNY)
- Typical swing, my own rough estimate: USD/CNY's realized volatility is usually about 2.5% to 4% annualized. Over 16 trading days, that gives a standard deviation of about 0.6% to 0.9%. Moves larger than ±1.5% in three weeks are rare and usually come from a policy shock.
- The PBOC actively leans against fast moves through its daily fixing, which limits the extremes on both sides.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question.
- May 2026: HSBC moved its year-end forecast to 6.65 (from 6.75). Deutsche Bank's base case is 6.55 at end-2026. Goldman Sachs has a 12-month target of about 6.7, or 6.70 to 6.80 by year-end. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/currencies/articles/global-banks-raise-yuan-forecasts-075406057.html)
- Late 2025: The Reuters poll average for end-2026 was 6.92, already passed. [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/global-investment-houses-forecast-chinese-yuan-rising-past-key-7-mark-in-2026-ce7d51d8d98af12c)
- Most bank targets sit near or below the current spot level, which points to more yuan strength. These forecasts are months old.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Daily PBOC fixings, about 9:15 Beijing time. The key question is whether the stronger-fix trend continues or the PBOC starts resisting again.
- About Sept 23 to 25: a Trump-Xi leaders' summit in Washington. Its outcome could move the yuan either way. [Arise](https://www.arise.tv/yuan-climbs-to-three-year-high-as-china-eases-resistance-to-currency-gains-ahead-of-trump-xi-summit/)
- Sept 30: China's official PMIs.
- Oct 1 to 8: Golden Week, with the onshore market closed.
- Oct 2: US September jobs report. It matters for whether the Fed hikes again and for the dollar.
- Around Oct 7 to 8: China's September FX reserves, plus the minutes of the Fed's Sept 16 meeting.
- Quarter-end corporate dollar selling and seasonal exporter conversion.
